title: Solving an Equation Defined Piecewise
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For $f(x)=x+2$ when $x<0$ and $f(x)=x^{2}$ when $x\ge 0$, find every real $x$ satisfying $f(x)=1$.

steps.title: Solve Inside the Negative Branch
steps.explanation: On $x<0$ set the linear formula equal to $1$, obtaining $x=-1$.
steps.why: Each branch generates its own candidate solution set.

steps.title: Validate the First Candidate
steps.explanation: The candidate $-1$ lies in the branch's stated domain, so it is a genuine solution.
steps.why: Solutions found on a branch must be tested against that branch's restriction.

steps.title: Solve Inside the Quadratic Branch
steps.explanation: On $x\\ge 0$ the equation becomes $x^2=1$, whose algebraic roots are $1$ and $-1$.
steps.why: A quadratic target produces two roots before domain filtering.

steps.title: Filter by the Branch Domain
steps.explanation: Only $x=1$ satisfies $x\\ge 0$; the root $-1$ falls outside this branch and is discarded (it is already accounted for by the first branch).
steps.why: The solution set of a piecewise equation is the union of branch solutions that pass their own domain tests.
